questions.prompt: An array is initialized and modified as shown. Which four elements does it contain afterward, in sequence? Arrange the resulting values in order.
questions.explanation: shift removes 20, pop removes 80, push adds 10 at the end, and unshift adds 100 at the front. The final array is [100, 40, 60, 10].

questions.prompt: For a finite Number value with absolute value below 10^21 and an integer digits from 3 through 100, choose the function that returns a string formatted with exactly digits decimal places.
questions.explanation: toFixed(digits) returns a string formatted with the specified number of decimal places for the stated range. toPrecision counts significant digits and toString interprets its argument as a radix. Binary floating-point representation can affect rounding.

questions.prompt: Analyze the following code fragment. Line numbers are for reference only. For each statement, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.

pairs.left: The call to multiply on line 09 returns 100.
When getProduct() is invoked, its call to multiply on line 19 returns 100.

questions.explanation: The outer multiply reads 25 and 4, returning 100. When getProduct is invoked, its nested multiply reads the local 2 and 3, returning 6. Merely declaring getProduct does not execute its body.

questions.prompt: Create a JavaScript function that accepts a number of months to add to or subtract from the current date and returns the adjusted Date. Complete the three code segments. More than one first-row construction is valid; either is accepted. value is an integer and standard Date overflow behavior is intended.
questions.explanation: Both new Date() and new Date create a current Date when no arguments are passed, so both first-row choices are accepted. Date() without new returns a string. getMonth() reads the zero-based local month and setMonth(month + value) adjusts it. End-of-month overflow follows Date rules rather than clamping to the last day.
questions.answerLabel: var date = new Date(); / var month = date.getMonth(); / date.setMonth(month + value);

pairs.left: [2] Add a number to the array

questions.prompt: Write a program that advises a person to ride a bike when the temperature is above 65 degrees and it is not raining. Otherwise, advise taking the train if the car has half a tank of gas or less, and driving the car when it has more fuel. Complete the source’s conditional structure.
questions.explanation: && requires both warm weather and no rain. Only when that condition fails does the <= .5 fuel check choose the train; more fuel selects driving.

questions.prompt: Create ticketPrice(age). Customers younger than 5 or at least 65 enter free. Customers aged 5 through 17 pay $10 USD; everyone else pays $20 USD. Complete the conditions.
questions.explanation: age < 5 || age >= 65 covers both free groups. age >= 5 && age < 18 covers ages 5 through 17. The remaining ages keep the default price of 20.

questions.prompt: Create a safe-division check with numerator and denominator parameters. It should return false when the denominator is zero and true otherwise. Review the code, then select Yes or No for each statement. Assume both parameters are finite numbers.

questions.prompt: Variable x has the value 5 and variable y has the value 7. Select True if each expression evaluates to true. Otherwise, select False.
questions.explanation: With x = 5 and y = 7, both comparisons joined by && are true; neither equality joined by || is true; x !== 7 is true; and negating x == y gives true.
